The specification describes the Spring Framework and lists 8 user stories related to Spring XD modules being moved/ported to the s-c-s (Spring Cloud Stream) repo. The user stories are:

U1: Move mqtt module from XD to s-c-s repo (as sink)
U2: Move null module from XD to s-c-s repo (as sink)
U3: Move shell module from XD to s-c-s repo (as sink)
U4: Move splunk module from XD to s-c-s repo (as sink)
U5: Move tcp module from XD to s-c-s repo (as sink)
U6: Move jdbc module from XD to s-c-s repo (as source)
U7: Port aggregator module from XD to s-c-s repo (as processor)
U8: Port http-client module from XD to s-c-s repo (as processor)

   - Code migration/porting

- Project setup: 1 day
- Common test infrastructure: 2 days
- Documentation/templates: 1 day

technical_and_design_decisions: Treat the 8 user stories as independent module migrations/ports from Spring XD to Spring Cloud Stream (s-c-s); each becomes a separate Gradle sub-module under the s-c-s repository.

For 'move' user stories (U1–U6) the existing XD module code is largely copied and repackaged, with dependency updates and adaptation to the s-c-s channel binding API; for 'port' stories (U7, U8) deeper refactoring is required because the modules were originally not processor-style.
Use Spring Cloud Stream's @EnableBinding / functional binding style to expose module inputs/outputs, replacing XD's Module-style adapters.
Reuse Spring XD's existing module options metadata, translating them to s-c-s module configuration properties.
Adopt Java 17 and Spring Framework 6.x as required by the project baseline.
Test strategy combines JUnit 5 unit tests for option parsing/binding logic and Spring Cloud Stream integration tests using embedded test binders for end-to-end behavior.
Common module packaging (jar layout, manifest, Spring auto-configuration registration) is implemented once and shared across the 8 modules via a parent pom/gradle script.
Documentation is generated from a common template (README + option reference) reused for all 8 modules.
assumptions: The 'single developer' is experienced with both Spring XD internals and Spring Cloud Stream, so no ramp-up/training time is included.
Source code of the original Spring XD modules is available and may be reused verbatim or with minimal changes for the 'move' stories.
The literal token {{null}} in U2 refers to the actual Spring XD 'null' sink module (a module that simply consumes and discards messages); it is not a missing field.
Each module already has well-defined behavior in XD, so the goal is functional equivalence in s-c-s, not redesign.
No new infrastructure work (CI, repository creation, license headers) beyond what is needed to make the modules build and pass tests in the s-c-s repo.
A 1 workday = 8 hours of focused development effort; estimates exclude meetings, code review turnaround time, and unrelated overhead.
Integration testing uses embedded/in-memory brokers where possible (e.g., embedded MQTT broker, H2 for JDBC, mock HTTP server), so no external test infrastructure provisioning is required.
Per-module effort includes code migration, unit tests, and one end-to-end integration test, but excludes long-running soak or performance tests.

activities.activity_description: Create the multi-module project layout in the s-c-s repo, configure the parent build (Gradle), set up shared dependency management, common auto-configuration plumbing for s-c-s modules, and a shared test harness base class.
Move the XD mqtt sink module into s-c-s: translate options, wire input channel binding, adapt MQTT client integration, write unit and integration tests using an embedded MQTT broker.
Move the XD 'null' sink module into s-c-s: trivial consumer that discards incoming messages; implement binding, options, and basic tests.
Move the XD shell sink module into s-c-s: invoke external shell commands per incoming message; port ProcessBuilder logic, options, and tests.
Move the XD splunk sink module into s-c-s: port HTTP-based Splunk HEC integration, options (host, token, index, etc.), and tests using a mock HTTP server.
Move the XD tcp sink module into s-c-s: port TCP client/reactor-based connection handling, serialization options, and tests using a local embedded TCP server.
Move the XD jdbc source module into s-c-s: port polling/JDBC query execution, row-mapping options, scheduled trigger, and tests using H2 with a populated schema.
Port the XD aggregator module into s-c-s as a processor: implement aggregation window, release strategies, correlation modes, options, and tests covering both time- and size-based windows.
Port the XD http-client module into s-c-s as a processor: implement request building, response handling, expected-response-status options, and tests using a mock HTTP server (MockWebServer).

Build and run an end-to-end streaming pipeline test that exercises representative modules together (e.g., jdbc source → aggregator → http-client processor → mqtt sink) to validate binding compatibility and message flow.
Write per-module README and option reference using the shared template, update the s-c-s top-level documentation index, and prepare release notes / changelog entries for the 8 modules.
